expectations.text: Article is 700–800 words including proof blocks
expectations.evidence: The reader-facing article is 1,548 whitespace-delimited words including proof blocks, exceeding the 800-word maximum.
The article says on-device permission, keyboard, and background states made continuity decisive and directly led to rejecting the calendar-first direction in favor of the conversational composer.

expectations.text: No more than two detailed decisions
expectations.evidence: Despite its excessive length, the article develops two substantive decision arcs: selection of the scheduling model and creation of the bounded requirements-check assistant. Prototype fidelity is presented as the method used to resolve the primary product decision.
The article states that the work resolved a direction 'before launch' and explicitly disclaims adoption, engagement, market performance, and measured review improvement.
The article contains five Markdown proof blocks: 'Constraint', 'Experiment', 'Decision', 'Insight', and 'Workflow spin-off', exceeding the maximum of four.

suggestions.assertion: No more than two detailed decisions
suggestions.reason: 'Detailed decision' has no objective boundary. Name the allowed decision arcs or define a structural test, such as no more than two sections that present a choice, rationale, and selected outcome.
Clarify whether a clearly labeled hypothetical 'Next signal' counts toward the block limit or whether every counted block must have observed or author-reported evidence.

eval_feedback.overall: The length and block-count checks distinguish the versions, but two assertions need tighter operational definitions.
